newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese finmin sees inflation slowing after Q1.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese finmin sees inflation slowing after Q1.

text.p: Portugal's inflation rate should remain steady in the first quarter of 1997 and then begin to slow towards the government's end of year target of 2.25-2.5 percent, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Wednesday.
"You can say that in the first quarter we will experience a stabilisation...from April we can expect a decline," Sousa Franco told journalists, reaffirming a forecast recently issued by his ministry.
"Everything points to the goal being reached," he added.
The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent month-on-month in January to take the year-on-year to 3.3 percent and the rolling 12-month average, the government benchmark, to 3.2 percent.
"Things went better than we expected in January," the minister said.
